subproblem.title: Null-set consequences of the co-area identity: G = 0 a.e. on each level set, and null subsets of M have null slices (parent Steps 1–2; Simon Ch. 6, proof of 4.5(2))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ and ν be measures on ℝ^P, let M ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set, and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be Borel measurable. Assume the co-area identity (CA): for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], the function t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dν is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dν dt = ∫_M |G| g dμ. Integrals over M ∩ f⁻¹{t} and over M are taken against the restricted measures, which are defined for arbitrary sets. Then: (i) for every c ∈ ℝ and μ⌞M-a.e. x, f(x) = c implies G(x) = 0; (ii) for every Z ⊆ M with μ(Z) = 0, ν(Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 for Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ ℝ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Steps 1 and 2. Step 1 is Simon's remark after (4) in the proof of Ch. 6, Lemma 4.5(2): ∇^M f = 0 Hⁿ-a.e. on {x ∈ M : f(x) = c} for every constant c. Step 2 is the null-transfer property used for the slice triple. Both are stated for arbitrary measures μ, ν. The parent takes μ = H^{m+1}, ν = H^m, and (CA) is the conclusion of its sibling dependency slicing_im_coarea, which has exactly this shape.

Notation. For S ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_S h dν is the integral against the restricted measure ν⌞S. This is defined for arbitrary S. For a Borel set A and an arbitrary S, ∫_S 1_A dν = (ν⌞S)(A) = ν(A ∩ S). L¹ denotes Lebesgue measure on ℝ. (CA) is the hypothesis: for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dν is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dν dt = ∫_M |G| g dμ.

Part (i). Fix c ∈ ℝ.
1. A_c := f⁻¹{c} is Borel because f is Borel. Apply (CA) to g := 1_{A_c}. With φ_c(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} 1_{A_c} dν this gives ∫_ℝ φ_c(t) dt = ∫_M |G|·1_{A_c} dμ.
2. For t ≠ c, φ_c(t) = ν(A_c ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{t})) = ν(∅) = 0, because no x has both f(x) = c and f(x) = t.
3. The singleton {c} is L¹-null, so φ_c = 0 L¹-a.e. Hence ∫_ℝ φ_c dt = 0.
4. Therefore ∫_M |G|·1_{A_c} dμ = 0. The integrand x ↦ |G(x)|·1_{A_c}(x) is a nonnegative Borel function (G and f are Borel). A nonnegative measurable function with zero integral vanishes almost everywhere, so |G(x)|·1_{A_c}(x) = 0 for μ⌞M-a.e. x.
5. At such an x with f(x) = c we have 1_{A_c}(x) = 1, so |G(x)| = 0, i.e. G(x) = 0. This proves (i).
Part (ii). Let Z ⊆ M with μ(Z) = 0.
6. Choose a Borel set Z' ⊇ Z with μ(Z') = μ(Z) = 0, e.g. the measurable hull (toMeasurable).
7. Apply (CA) to g := 1_{Z'}. Then ψ(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} 1_{Z'} dν = ν(Z' ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{t})) is L¹-a.e.-measurable, and ∫_ℝ ψ dt = ∫_M |G|·1_{Z'} dμ.
8. Since μ(Z') = 0, 1_{Z'} = 0 μ-a.e., hence also μ⌞M-a.e. (μ⌞M ≤ μ). So the right side of step 7 is 0.
9. ψ ≥ 0 is a.e.-measurable with ∫ψ = 0, so ψ(t) = 0 for L¹-a.e. t.
10. For such t, Z ∩ f⁻¹{t} ⊆ Z' ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{t}), because Z ⊆ Z' and Z ⊆ M. Hence ν(Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ≤ ψ(t) = 0. This proves (ii). ∎

    ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ ν : Measure (Eucl P)) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (G : Eucl P → Eucl P), Measurable f → Measurable G → (∀ g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → AEMeasurable (fun t : ℝ => ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂ν) (volume : Measure ℝ) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂ν) ∂(volume : Measure ℝ) = ∫⁻ x in M, ‖G x‖ₑ * g x ∂μ) → (∀ c : ℝ, ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict M), f x = c → G x = 0) ∧ ∀ Z : Set (Eucl P), Z ⊆ M → μ Z = 0 → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ν (Z ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}) = 0 := by
  intro P μ ν M f G hf hG CA
  constructor
  · intro c
    have hmc : MeasurableSet (f ⁻¹' {c}) := hf (measurableSet_singleton c)
    obtain ⟨-, hCA⟩ := CA ((f ⁻¹' {c}).indicator 1) (measurable_one.indicator hmc)
    -- the slice integrals vanish for `t ≠ c`
    have hslice : ∀ t, t ≠ c → ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, (f ⁻¹' {c}).indicator 1 x ∂ν = 0 := by
      intro t ht
      rw [lintegral_indicator_one hmc, Measure.restrict_apply hmc]
      convert measure_empty (μ := ν)
      ext x
      simp only [mem_inter_iff, mem_preimage, mem_singleton_iff, mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false,
        not_and]
      intro hxc _ hxt
      exact ht (hxt.symm.trans hxc)
    have hL : ∫⁻ t, (∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, (f ⁻¹' {c}).indicator 1 x ∂ν) ∂(volume : Measure ℝ) = 0 := by
      have : (fun t => ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, (f ⁻¹' {c}).indicator 1 x ∂ν) =ᵐ[volume] 0 := by
        have hne : ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ≠ c := by
          simp [ae_iff, measure_singleton]
        filter_upwards [hne] with t ht
        exact hslice t ht
      rw [lintegral_congr_ae this]
      simp
    rw [hL] at hCA
    have hmeas : AEMeasurable (fun x => ‖G x‖ₑ * (f ⁻¹' {c}).indicator 1 x) (μ.restrict M) :=
      (hG.enorm.mul (measurable_one.indicator hmc)).aemeasurable
    have h0 := (lintegral_eq_zero_iff' hmeas).1 hCA.symm
    filter_upwards [h0] with x hx hfx
    have hxc : x ∈ f ⁻¹' {c} := hfx
    simp only [Pi.zero_apply, indicator_of_mem hxc, Pi.one_apply, mul_one, enorm_eq_zero] at hx
    exact hx

      simp
    rw [hR] at hCA
    have h0 := (lintegral_eq_zero_iff' hae).1 hCA
    filter_upwards [h0] with t ht
    simp only [Pi.zero_apply] at ht
    rw [lintegral_indicator_one hZ'm, Measure.restrict_apply hZ'm] at ht

subproblem.title: Tangential gradient of the piecewise-linear level cut-off h_ε = ψ_ε∘f (parent Step 7; Simon Ch. 6, proof of 4.5(2), (4))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P, and let Tan(x, Q) be an arbitrary predicate on points x ∈ ℝ^P and linear subspaces Q ⊆ ℝ^P. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz (L ≥ 0), let G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be Borel with |G(x)| ≤ L for every x, and let t ∈ ℝ and ε > 0. Assume (TG): for μ-a.e. x and every Q with Tan(x, Q), G(x) ∈ Q and, for every u ∈ Q, s ↦ f(x + su) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0. Assume also that for μ-a.e. x, f(x) = t − ε implies G(x) = 0, and that for μ-a.e. x, f(x) = t implies G(x) = 0. Put h_ε(x) := max(0, min(1, (t − f(x))/ε)) and G_ε := 1_{f⁻¹((t−ε,t))}·(−ε⁻¹G). Then there is K ≥ 0 with four properties: h_ε is K-Lipschitz; G_ε is Borel; |G_ε(x)| ≤ K for every x; and for μ-a.e. x and every Q with Tan(x, Q), G_ε(x) ∈ Q and, for every u ∈ Q, s ↦ h_ε(x + su) has derivative ⟨G_ε(x), u⟩ at s = 0.

subproblem.title: Signed co-area identity on bands {a < f < b} and integrability of the slice density (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 4.2; parent Step 4)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ and ν be measures on ℝ^P, and let M ⊆ ℝ^P. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and g : ℝ^P → ℝ be Borel, with x ↦ |G(x)|·g(x) integrable for μ⌞M. Assume the co-area identity (CA): for every Borel h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} h dν is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} h dν dt = ∫_M |G| h dμ (integrals against restricted measures). Let φ(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dν be the Bochner integral against ν⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}), which is 0 if g is not integrable there. Then φ is Lebesgue-integrable on ℝ, and for all a, b ∈ ℝ, ∫_{M∩f⁻¹((a,b))} |G| g dμ = ∫_{(a,b)} φ(t) dt.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 4, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, Remark 4.2: replace g in the co-area formula of Lemma 4.1 by g times the characteristic function of a band in f to get ∫_{M∩{f<t}} |∇^M f| g dHⁿ = ∫_{−∞}^{t} ∫_{M_s} g dH^{n−1} ds. Here it is written out for a signed L¹ density, with arbitrary measures μ, ν and an open band (a, b). The parent takes μ = H^{m+1}, ν = H^m, and its sibling slicing_im_coarea supplies (CA).

Notation. ∫_S denotes integration against the restricted measure (defined for every S ⊆ ℝ^P). (CA) is the hypothesis: for every Borel h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} h dν is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} h dν dt = ∫_M |G| h dμ. Put g⁺ := ofReal(g) and g⁻ := ofReal(−g); both are [0, ∞]-valued and Borel. For real x, ofReal(x) + ofReal(−x) = |x|. Put φ₊(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g⁺ dν and φ₋(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g⁻ dν, both in [0, ∞]. φ(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dν is the Bochner integral, which is 0 when g is not integrable there.

1. (Products.) Since |G(x)| ≥ 0, ofReal(|G(x)|·g(x)) = |G(x)|·g⁺(x) and ofReal(−|G(x)|·g(x)) = |G(x)|·g⁻(x), with |G(x)| read as an extended nonnegative number.
2. (Finiteness.) By (CA) with h = g^±, φ_± is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ φ_± dt = ∫_M |G|·g^± dμ = ∫_M ofReal(±|G|g) dμ. This is ≤ ∫_M ||G|g| dμ, which is finite because |G|g is μ⌞M-integrable. Hence φ_±(t) < ∞ for L¹-a.e. t.
3. (Slice integrability.) Let t satisfy φ₊(t) < ∞ and φ₋(t) < ∞. Then ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} |g| dν = φ₊(t) + φ₋(t) < ∞, because |g| = g⁺ + g⁻ and the lower integral is additive (g⁺ is measurable). Since g is Borel, g is integrable for ν⌞(M∩f⁻¹{t}). Splitting into positive and negative parts gives φ(t) = φ₊(t).toReal − φ₋(t).toReal.
4. (φ is integrable.) Put ψ(t) := φ₊(t).toReal − φ₋(t).toReal. Each φ_±.toReal is L¹-integrable: φ_± is a.e.-measurable with finite integral (step 2). So ψ is integrable. By step 3, φ = ψ L¹-a.e., so φ is integrable. This is the first conclusion.
5. (Band identity for a nonnegative Borel h.) Fix a, b ∈ ℝ and let E := f⁻¹((a, b)), a Borel set. Let h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] be Borel and apply (CA) to 1_E·h.
 (a) Fix t. The set {x : f(x) ≠ t} is Borel and ν({f ≠ t} ∩ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = ν(∅) = 0. So f(x) = t for ν⌞(M∩f⁻¹{t})-a.e. x. For such x, 1_E(x) = 1_{(a,b)}(t). Hence ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} 1_E h dν = 1_{(a,b)}(t)·∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} h dν.
 (b) So the left side of (CA) is ∫_ℝ 1_{(a,b)}(t)·∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} h dν dt = ∫_{(a,b)} ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} h dν dt.
 (c) For the right side, |G|·1_E h = 1_E·(|G|h). The restriction of μ⌞M to the Borel set E is μ⌞(E ∩ M), so ∫_M |G| 1_E h dμ = ∫_{M∩E} |G| h dμ.
 Hence ∫_{M∩E} |G| h dμ = ∫_{(a,b)} ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} h dν dt.
6. (Left side of the claim.) |G|g is μ⌞(M∩E)-integrable, being the restriction of a μ⌞M-integrable function. So, splitting into positive and negative parts and using step 1:
 ∫_{M∩E} |G| g dμ = (∫_{M∩E} |G| g⁺ dμ).toReal − (∫_{M∩E} |G| g⁻ dμ).toReal.
 By step 5 with h = g⁺ and h = g⁻, this equals (∫_{(a,b)} φ₊ dt).toReal − (∫_{(a,b)} φ₋ dt).toReal.
7. (Right side of the claim.) Since φ = ψ a.e., ∫_{(a,b)} φ = ∫_{(a,b)} ψ = ∫_{(a,b)} φ₊.toReal − ∫_{(a,b)} φ₋.toReal, both terms being integrable. Each φ_± is a.e.-measurable and a.e. finite on (a, b), so ∫_{(a,b)} φ_±.toReal = (∫_{(a,b)} φ_±).toReal.
8. Steps 6 and 7 give ∫_{M∩f⁻¹((a,b))} |G| g dμ = ∫_{(a,b)} φ(t) dt for all a, b. If a ≥ b, both sides are integrals over empty sets and equal 0. ∎

Then for Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dν = ∫_{{x ∈ M : f(x) = t, x ∈ S}} F dν (Bochner integrals against the restricted measures).

Source: parent proof, Step 5 (identification of the slice density with tauAction on M_t, using the null-transfer property NT). It is stated abstractly for measures μ, ν, a μ-null-measurable M and a Borel set S. The parent takes μ = H^{m+1}, ν = H^m, S = {G ≠ 0} and F = θ·ξ_t(ω); NT comes from the sibling coarea_null (ii).

This step closes a measure-theoretic gap in the supplied Step 5. The slice M ∩ f⁻¹{t} need not be ν-measurable. For a non-measurable set A the restricted measure ν⌞A can charge points outside A, so "g = F at every point of A outside a ν-null set" does not by itself give g = F ν⌞A-a.e. The proof below therefore first replaces M by a Borel M₁ ⊆ M with μ(M ∖ M₁) = 0, and uses NT to see that the restricted measures do not change for a.e. t.

Notation. ∫_A h dν is the Bochner integral against ν⌞A, defined for every A ⊆ ℝ^P (it is 0 if h is not integrable). Two integrands that agree ν⌞A-a.e. have the same integral, whether or not they are measurable or integrable. A =ᵐ B means ν((A ∖ B) ∪ (B ∖ A)) = 0; it implies ν⌞A = ν⌞B.

1. (Null subsets of M.) Let Z₁ := M ∩ {x : x ∈ S and g(x) ≠ F(x)}. For every set D, μ(D ∩ M) ≤ (μ⌞M)(D). With D := {x : ¬(x ∈ S ⟹ g(x) = F(x))}, which is μ⌞M-null by hypothesis, this gives μ(Z₁) = 0. Since M is μ-null-measurable, there is a Borel M₁ ⊆ M with M₁ = M μ-a.e.; put Z₂ := M ∖ M₁, so μ(Z₂) = 0. Then Z := Z₁ ∪ Z₂ ⊆ M and μ(Z) = 0.
2. (Good t.) By NT, ν(Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 for L¹-a.e. t. Fix such a t. Since f is Borel, f⁻¹{t} is Borel.
3. (Borel replacements of the domains.)
 - Let A := M ∩ f⁻¹{t} and A₁ := M₁ ∩ f⁻¹{t}, which is Borel. Then A₁ ⊆ A and A ∖ A₁ ⊆ Z₂ ∩ f⁻¹{t} ⊆ Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}, which is ν-null. So A =ᵐ A₁ and ν⌞A = ν⌞A₁.
 - Let B := {x : x ∈ M, f(x) = t, x ∈ S} and B₁ := A₁ ∩ S, which is Borel. Then B₁ ⊆ B and B ∖ B₁ ⊆ Z₂ ∩ f⁻¹{t}, so ν⌞B = ν⌞B₁.
4. (Left side.) g = 0 off S, so g = 1_S·g everywhere. As S is Borel, ∫_A g dν = ∫_{A₁} 1_S g dν = ∫_{A₁∩S} g dν = ∫_{B₁} g dν.
5. (g = F on B₁.) If x ∈ B₁ and g(x) ≠ F(x), then x ∈ M, x ∈ S, g(x) ≠ F(x) and f(x) = t. So x ∈ Z₁ ∩ f⁻¹{t} ⊆ Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}. Thus {x ∈ B₁ : g(x) ≠ F(x)} is ν-null. Since B₁ is Borel, this means g = F ν⌞B₁-a.e., and so ∫_{B₁} g dν = ∫_{B₁} F dν.
6. (Conclusion.) ∫_A g dν = ∫_{B₁} g dν = ∫_{B₁} F dν = ∫_B F dν, using steps 4, 5 and 3. This holds for every t as in step 2, i.e. for L¹-a.e. t. ∎

For w ∈ ℝ^P and an m-covector α, w♭∧α := alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ w).smulRight α), an (m+1)-covector. This map is bilinear in (w, α). ξ_t(x) := ξ(x) ∘ alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ∘ smulRightL(innerSL ν(x)); by definition (rfl), ξ_t(x)(α) = ξ(x)(ν(x)♭∧α). All "a.e." statements are for μ⌞M.

1. (Facts about ω.) ω ∈ D^m(U) is smooth, has compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U. So ω is continuous, K is compact, K ⊆ U, and K is closed, hence Borel. ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ K. Since ω is continuous with compact support, there is C_ω ≥ 0 with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C_ω for all x.
2. (Borel version of θ on M ∩ K.) By IsRectifiableTriple.integrableOn applied to the compact K ⊆ U, θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ K. In particular θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞(M ∩ K), so there is a Borel θ' with θ = θ' μ⌞(M∩K)-a.e. As K is Borel, μ⌞(M∩K) = (μ⌞M)⌞K. Hence for μ⌞M-a.e. x: x ∈ K ⟹ θ(x) = θ'(x).
3. (Borel version of ξ.) By IsRectifiableTriple.aestronglyMeasurable there is a strongly measurable ξ' with ξ = ξ' μ⌞M-a.e.
4. (Unit bound, Fact U.) By IsRectifiableTriple.orients, for μ⌞M-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ : Fin (m+1) → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. By the sibling unit_bound (fiw_ims_tt_unit_bound), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every (m+1)-covector α, for μ⌞M-a.e. x.
5. (The field β := ν♭∧ω.) ν is Borel, since G and x ↦ |G(x)|⁻¹ are, and |ν(x)| ≤ 1 (it is 1 if G(x) ≠ 0 and 0 otherwise). The map (w, α) ↦ w♭∧α is continuous: it is the bounded bilinear map (λ, α) ↦ λ.smulRight α, precomposed with innerSL in the first argument and followed by the continuous linear map alternatizeUncurryFinCLM. So β(x) := ν(x)♭∧ω(x) is strongly measurable, as a continuous image of the strongly measurable pair (ν, ω). Moreover ‖β(x)‖ ≤ (m+1)·‖(innerSL ν(x)).smulRight ω(x)‖ = (m+1)|ν(x)|‖ω(x)‖ ≤ (m+1)C_ω. Evaluation (Λ, α) ↦ Λ(α) is continuous, so x ↦ ξ'(x)(β(x)) is strongly measurable.

7. (Integrability.) 1_K θ' is μ⌞M-integrable. Indeed, for Borel K, 1_Kθ' is μ⌞M-integrable iff θ' is integrable for (μ⌞M)⌞K = μ⌞(M∩K), and θ' = θ a.e. there with θ integrable on M ∩ K (step 2). For μ⌞M-a.e. x (steps 3 and 4):
 - if x ∈ S, then |g(x)| = |θ'(x)|·|ξ(x)(β(x))| ≤ |θ'(x)|·‖β(x)‖ ≤ (m+1)C_ω·|1_Kθ'(x)|;
 - if x ∉ S, then |g(x)| = 0 ≤ (m+1)C_ω·|1_Kθ'(x)|.
 g is measurable and a.e. dominated by an integrable function, so g is μ⌞M-integrable.
8. (Identity (a).) Let x lie in the μ⌞M-conull set where ξ(x) = ξ'(x) and (x ∈ K ⟹ θ(x) = θ'(x)). Suppose G(x) ≠ 0. Then ξ_t(x)(ω(x)) = ξ(x)(ν(x)♭∧ω(x)) = ξ(x)(β(x)).
 - If x ∈ K, then g(x) = θ'(x)ξ'(x)(β(x)) = θ(x)ξ(x)(β(x)).
 - If x ∉ K, then ω(x) = 0, so β(x) = 0 and θ(x)ξ(x)(β(x)) = 0 = g(x).
 In both cases g(x) = θ(x)·ξ_t(x)(ω(x)).
9. (Identity (b).) For the same x:
 - If G(x) = 0, then G(x)♭∧ω(x) = 0 (innerSL 0 = 0, 0.smulRight α = 0, and alternatizeUncurryFin is linear). So θ(x)ξ(x)(G(x)♭∧ω(x)) = θ(x)ξ(x)(0) = 0 = |G(x)|·g(x).
 - If G(x) ≠ 0, then G(x) = |G(x)|·ν(x). Linearity of w ↦ w♭∧α gives G(x)♭∧ω(x) = |G(x)|·β(x). So θ(x)ξ(x)(G(x)♭∧ω(x)) = |G(x)|·θ(x)ξ(x)(β(x)) = |G(x)|·g(x), by step 8.
 Hence (a) and (b) hold for μ⌞M-a.e. x. ∎
